_about: Catalogue of unsolved historical ciphers not on the Tomokiyo, Schmeh or Dunin lists. Scores are 1-5 and unvalidated: importance = historical weight of what the text could add; solvability = odds of a full reading with the material available online; difficulty = technical work needed (1 trivial key alignment, 5 statistics-only on an unknown system). Priority is computed on the page from adjustable weights. Class A = siblings with decipherment in the same volume, B = partial key or known family in print, C = no key, no sibling. seen: image = leaf viewed on the Gallica image; catalogue = selected from the catalogue description only. outcome: 'attempted, open' once an entry has been taken to the leaf here without a reading. Entries read, partly read, resolved or found already in print are removed from this file (19 Sept 2026) and recorded in SOLVED_CATALOGUE.md; ids are not reused.

entries.title: Hieronimo Ranzo (?) to 'Garbino', intercepted imperial letter
entries.shelfmark: BnF fr. 3022 no. 20 (ff. 44r–46v; addition sheet and jargon ff. 48–50v)
entries.status: The other two items first catalogued here (nos. 6 and 10, del Vasto to Charles V) are read: no. 10 by Lasry (2023) with Tomokiyo's edited text, no. 6 in vasto1527/n6_reading.md. No. 20 is an Italian letter, Madrid 11 Apr 1528, to 'Garbino', in the same code as Hieronimo Ranzo's letters (fr. 2988). The code is initial letter + number with non-alphabetical numbering; ~3,900 groups are transcribed, but only the function-word skeleton is recoverable without the key. No French decipherment exists; Clair. 327 ff. 279-280 is an undeciphered copy.
entries.why: Five months after the Sack of Rome, during Lautrec's campaign in Italy.
entries.score_note: Large one-part-looking code, one letter, no key; see vasto1527/NOTES.md.
entries.verify: Look for Ranzo's key or a deciphered Ranzo letter (Simancas, Vienna HHStA) before any statistical attack.

entries.title: Catherine de Médicis and the Court to the bishop of Rennes
entries.correspondents: Catherine de Médicis; Charles IX's Court; Bourdin → Bernardin Bochetel, bishop of Rennes
entries.shelfmark: BnF fr. 3181 f. 55; 500 Colbert 390 pp. 139, 357; 500 Colbert 392 p. 231
entries.folio_note: fr. 3181: folio = Gallica view + 19, so f. 55 = view 36, f. 57 = view 38. 500 Colbert 390 = btv1b10033942k (p. 139 = view 70, p. 357 = view 180); 500 Colbert 392 = btv1b100339594 (p. 231 = view 112).
entries.status: Read in part, 20 Sept 2026. fr. 3181 f. 55 (31 July 1563) had never been deciphered: La Ferrière printed the letter in 1885 (Lettres de Catherine de Médicis II, pp. 79-81, from this folio) with the thirteen ciphered lines set as an empty bracket footnoted "Partie chiffrée", and Tomokiyo lists the folio as undeciphered. His reconstructed key for the Bishop of Rennes’ cipher (1561-64) does work on it, but only after being calibrated on this scribe’s hand against the sibling letter f. 57 (13 Aug 1563), which carries a line-by-line decipherment down its margin; its first ciphered line reads "que les princes". 401 signs transcribed from IIIF region requests at the native 8720x5935. About three fifths read, including "sceu ce que vous avez descouvert", "du mariage", "vostre advis", "d’iceulx en mon intention", "ayt tenu ce chemin", "vous mist en avant, qui l’avoit", "l’avancement du concile, à ce que", "de ce concile, mais nous", "avoir l’utilité qui en sortira", "mect des se[ss]ions". The enciphered subject is the Council of Trent and the Habsburg marriage, while the recovery of Le Havre in the same letter went in clear. Open: the remaining two fifths, blocked by near-identical r/s, e/l and o/h/t homophones in this hand rather than by the key; and the three siblings (500 Colbert 390 pp. 139 and 357, 392 p. 231), same cipher, still unread.
entries.why: Charles IX's majority declared at Rouen 17 Aug 1563; the last session of Trent.
entries.score_note: Reconstructed sibling keys exist; probably a variant or a key change. Content is Court instructions to an ambassador.
entries.verify: Test Tomokiyo's Rennes keys on f. 55 first.

entries.title: Papal-side letters: Sega, Baudouin-Desportes, Mauclerc
entries.correspondents: memoir → Cardinal Sega; Baudouin-Desportes → Pietro Aldobrandini and → Girolamo Frachetta; Dr Mauclerc → Creil
entries.status: Attempted 17 Sept 2026, not read. Tomokiyo's League polyphonic cipher (mayenne.htm) is the key; f. 188 (mostly clear, cipher on the verso) is the original of the deciphered f. 184-185, and f. 176 of f. 177. f. 186 is a clear letter with c. 58 lines of cipher passages, f. 189 one page wholly in cipher (33 lines): c. 5,000 polyphonic glyphs. A classifier trained on the 1,100 aligned glyphs of f. 188v reads 75-79 % of held-out glyphs, hand reading c. 70 %; the polyphonic decoder needs over 90 %, and no verbatim crib from f. 185 occurs in f. 189 or f. 186v (local-alignment search against a shuffled control). fr. 3985 no. 7 not examined.
entries.why: Written in the week of Henri IV's abjuration (25 Jul 1593) and the truce of Suresnes.
entries.score_note: Scores as first assigned; closed as not solvable with the present tools, see sega1593/NOTES.md.
entries.verify: Reopen with a paleographic transcription of f. 177 (to train on f. 176, 90 more lines) or a human glyph transcription of ff. 186/189; decoder and period LM are ready.

entries.title: Henri IV to Savary de Brèves (Constantinople)
entries.correspondents: Henri IV → François Savary de Brèves
entries.shelfmark: BnF fr. 3541 ff. 60-104 (twelve ciphered letters, Feb-Dec 1603); key fr. 3462 f. 103
entries.status: Plaintext known, 18 Sept 2026 (breves1603/): the original key is BnF fr. 3462 f. 103 (Gallica btv1b9058227h canvas 109). fr. 3541 (anc. Béthune 9021) holds twelve ciphered letters of 1603 (ff. 60-104). Berger de Xivrey, Lettres missives VI (1853), printed from a contemporary clear copy (Monmerqué ms 'Lettres à l'ambassadeur du Levant'): full text of 18 Feb (f. 60), 31 Mar (f. 63, not 1 Mar) and 17 Apr (f. 66), summaries of the nine others. Tomokiyo's partial f. 60 reading was corrected against it. The ciphertext itself is not digitised, so the letter-by-letter check of the nine summarised letters is blocked on BnF images. A second clear copy of all twelve is BnF fr. 4029 (register of 158 letters of Henri IV to Brèves, 1592-1608), nos. 131-142 on ff. 118-128, also not digitised: a reproduction of those folios gives the nine summarised letters in full with no decipherment. Brèves's own fr. 15578 f. 185 (Gallica btv1b9064568h canvas 196) is in the same cipher with an interlinear decipherment, for checking the key's signs.
entries.why: The Ottoman disorder of 1603 and the renewal of the Capitulations (1604).
entries.score_note: Partial key in print with sample readings; finishing it is table work.
entries.verify: Start from Tomokiyo's Brèves key; check fr. 3541 for further ciphered leaves.

entries.status: Read in part 18 Sept 2026 (orbais/): none of the three bound keys fits (no. 53 numerical, the letter has no figures; no. 61 an Italian key with other signs; no. 69 a League key with the square = e where the letter needs n). entries.title: King Frederick II (the Great) of Prussia (1712-1786) (London) to Louis Michell (1712-1786), Prussian resident in London
entries.correspondents: King Frederick II (the Great) of Prussia (1712-1786) → Louis Michell (1712-1786), Prussian resident in London
entries.shelfmark: KHA The Hague, Prins Willem V, inv.nr. 198
entries.status: DECODE R1955: Non-decrypted, 2 pp., nomenclator, numerical. 19 Sept 2026: transcribed in full (michell1751/transcription_r1955.txt). Heading "Lettre du Roi de Prusse au Secrétaire Michell du 28 Decemb. 1751", clear opening "Toutes vos dépêches m'ont été bien rendues et la dernière est du 14e de ce mois", 362 code groups (2 to 5346, with half-groups 1½, 10½, 40½, 150½, 180½, 660½), dated and signed Féderic. Only one letter of this date to Michell is in Politische Correspondenz 8 (no. 5263 = R1957), so this is the ministerial rescript and has no printed text. 295 of the 362 groups are distinct and the commonest occurs 5 times: a large two-part homophonic code, not breakable from this letter alone. It would need the Prussian ministerial code of 1751 (GStA), Lyonet's Dutch decipherments, or British decyphers of Michell's mail.

entries.title: Nicolo Sadoleto (Pozsony) to Ferdinand I / Ercole I d'Este, 4 ciphertexts
entries.correspondents: Nicolo Sadoleto → Ferdinand I / Ercole I d'Este
entries.shelfmark: ASMo, Ambasciatori b. 1/9, Envoy reports, Ferrara (4 items)
entries.status: Read in part 19 Sept 2026 (sadoleto1482/). The sign cipher (monoalphabetic with homophones, word divisions kept, 'quid' = perchè) was rebuilt from R1101 and R1104 against their contemporary clear copies on Vestigia (1283 = no. 7a; 1295 = 13a). R1101 and R1106 turn out to have been read at the time (7a; 26a/26b = Vestigia 1319, 4004). R1102 (16 Jul 1482), seven cipher lines with no clear copy, read in gist: the Venetian side's offer to Matthias of Veglia, a fleet command for his natural son János Corvin, and 100,000 a year. Open: one nomenclator group, the informant's title, a dozen signs; R1103's faded four-line block gives fragments only.
entries.why: The Ferrarese ambassador at Matthias Corvinus's court during the War of Ferrara (1482–84), when Ercole I d'Este's survival against Venice hung on Hungarian and Neapolitan support.
entries.score_note: Reviewed by hand 19 Sept 2026 from DECODE's metadata and the literature; leaf not viewed. Pre-1497: a reading would give the repo its oldest read cipher.
